principles: Grades use only stored fields and stored closes already in eval/tape_snapshots/<date>.json, plus index provider announcements recorded in eval/index_announcements.json.
The desk never computes a new indicator; the grader only reads stored fields and compares them to the fixed thresholds below.
A test is attached to a flag at registration and never changed afterwards; spec changes get a new spec_version and apply only to rows registered after the change.
Rows registered after the outcome window had already started are marked registered_retro: true and reported separately from live pre-registered calls.

thresholds.breakout: setup.direction == leading_uptrend AND setup.indicators.price_vs_50d_pct > 0 AND setup.indicators.relative_volume_20d > 1 AND setup.indicators.chaikin_money_flow_20d >= 0.10
thresholds.holds: gap > 10% (TAPE-06), thin dollar volume (FLOW-06), self-contradictory or stale row (FLOW-06), HKHC standing hold

stored_fields.as_of: as_of (row level; the session the row describes)
stored_fields.return_5d_pct: measures.return_5d_pct (stored close-to-close return over the 5 sessions ending at as_of)
stored_fields.benchmark_move_5d: context.market_move_5d_pct / context.beta_252d (stored beta-scaled benchmark move; see benchmark.fallback)

sessions.definition: A session is a trading day. The base session is the row as_of the desk read when it posted (row as_of in tape_snapshots/<run_date>.json, else the 'technical_summary as_of' date in the source string, else the trading day before run_date, marked base_as_of_inferred). Session k is the k-th trading day after the base.
sessions.calendar_us: NYSE trading days (weekdays minus NYSE holidays hard-coded in grade.py for 2026-2027).
sessions.calendar_non_us: Weekdays (approximation; recorded as calendar=weekday_approx in the numbers).
sessions.lookup: A session's numbers come from the first stored snapshot row whose as_of equals that session (point-in-time: earliest snapshot wins). A stale row (as_of earlier than the session) never stands in for the session.

benchmark.primary: SPY row (rows['SPY']) in the same tape_snapshots, close-to-close over the same base and end sessions.
benchmark.fallback: No SPY row is stored in tape_snapshots as of 2026-10-30. Until one is, the grader backs the stored 5-session SPY move out of the same end snapshot: median over SPY-benchmarked rows with as_of == end session and |beta_252d| >= 0.5 of context.market_move_5d_pct / context.beta_252d (requires >= 10 rows). On 2026-10-29/30 snapshots this is tight (IQR < 0.01 pct-pt), so it is the stored SPY move, not a new indicator. Only usable for 5-session windows.
benchmark.non_us: Rows whose stored benchmark is not SPY (e.g. 9984.T vs 1321.T, SAF.PA vs IEUR, .TO vs XIC.TO) are compared with their own stored benchmark move (that row's market_move_5d_pct / beta_252d, |beta| >= 0.5), else no_data. Reason: different session calendars make a same-window SPY comparison impossible from stored fields.
benchmark.fix_requested: Ask the snapshot routine owner to store the SPY row (and ideally a seeded random 20 of the full technical_summary) in every tape snapshot; the grader picks it up automatically.

pass_condition.plain: Pass if the name's close-to-close return from the base session to session 5 beats SPY's return over the same sessions.

persistence.plain: Next session: capitulation.state still in the capitulation set, and if the flag quoted RSI / stretch_z / trend_z / CMF, that field is still beyond the same threshold.

pass_condition.plain: RSI14 < 35 (incl. < 25) flags pass if the 5-session close-to-close return beats SPY's over the same sessions.

persistence.plain: Next session rsi_14 still below the band flagged (25 if the flag value was < 25, else 35).

pass_condition.plain: RSI14 > 70 flags pass if the 5-session close-to-close return trails SPY's over the same sessions.
Breakout flags pass if the close stays above the stored 50-day average (price_vs_50d_pct > 0) on each of the next 3 sessions' snapshots.

tests.benchmark: SPY context only (recorded, not used for pass/fail)

persistence.plain: Next session the full breakout rule is still met.

pass_condition.plain: 'Breakout lost' flags pass if the breakout rule is not met again on any of the next 3 sessions.

persistence.plain: Next session breakout rule still not met.

tests.note: Added (not in the suggested defaults) because run_log has 'breakout lost' rows (DDOG 10-13, SHOP 10-14).

pass_condition.plain: stretch_z / trend_z / CMF flags pass if (a) next session the same field is still beyond its threshold with the same sign AND (b) the sign of the 5-session close-to-close return agrees with the flag's direction (sign of the flagged value).

tests.benchmark: SPY excess return recorded alongside (not used for pass/fail)

persistence.plain: Next session |field| still beyond threshold with the same sign (also component (a) of the pass).

tests.note: Direction agreement follows the suggested default (continuation reading). Both raw return and excess return are stored so a mean-reversion reading can be scored later without regrading.

pass_condition.plain: Pass if the provider announces the predicted add / delete / migration for that exact index by the case deadline (FTSE Russell recon effective Dec 11 2026; S&P DJI quarterly rebalance Dec 19 2026). Fail (false flag) if the window closes without one. Pending until eval/index_announcements.json checked_through >= deadline.
A 'watch removed' call passes if no add to that index is announced by the next review deadline; fails if one is.

A flag reporting an already-announced event passes if a provider announcement for that ticker, exact index and action exists (FLOW-04 exact-index test); fails if announcements are checked through the run date and none matches.

held_names.plain: Held names (TAPE-06 gaps, FLOW-06 thin/self-contradictory/stale, HKHC) get the same test as the flag they would have been (counterfactual). The counterfactual kind is the kind of the logged flag text if the held row is in run_log; otherwise it is read from the held-date snapshot row by the fixed thresholds in this order: capitulation state, RSI < 35, RSI > 70, breakout rule, |stretch_z| > 2, |trend_z| > 1.25, |CMF| > 0.10. No snapshot row means no_data.

baseline.plain: For each run date, a seeded random sample of 20 names from that day's tape snapshot rows, excluding names flagged or held that day and SPY, graded with every return/breakout test over the same window, so each pass rate has a chance comparison.
baseline.pool: tape_snapshots/<run_date>.json rows with data_quality == 'ready'. Retro proxy when that snapshot does not exist: names logged in run_log on or before run_date (not flagged that day) that have a stored row at the window's end session.
baseline.z_baseline_note: Baseline for TA-Z-5D uses only component (b) (return sign vs direction), for each direction; flags must also persist, so this baseline is a lower bar.
baseline.known_bias: Snapshots hold only names the desk has flagged at some point (117-128 rows), not the full technical_summary, so the pool skews to high-volatility names.

grading.legacy_fields: grade / graded_on keep their existing meaning (next-snapshot persistence held/faded/no_data, used by the weekly scorecard). --daily fills them from persistence_grade only when they are null and never overwrites them. drew_verdict / verdict / verdict_by are never touched.
grading.no_data: Written when the window has closed (a later snapshot exists or 4 calendar days passed after the end session) and a needed snapshot row, close or benchmark is missing.
grading.never_regrade: A row whose test_grade (or persistence_grade) is already set is skipped.

report.groups: per rule id (lens_rules, else lens_rules_inferred; F/M aliases mapped) and per flag kind; live (registered_retro false) and retro reported separately
report.metrics: graded n, pass rate, baseline pass rate (same tests, same run dates), held counterfactual pass rate, persistence held/faded
report.under_review_candidate: rule with graded n >= 20 and pass rate <= baseline pass rate (computed on live, and separately on live+retro; never applied automatically - proposal to Drew only)

adjustments_from_suggested_defaults: SPY benchmark: no SPY row is stored yet; fallback backs the stored SPY 5-session move out of context.market_move_5d_pct / beta_252d in the same snapshot (documented above).
Non-US names use their own stored benchmark (different session calendars).
Added TA-BRKLOST-3S for 'breakout lost' rows, TA-IDX-NEG for 'watch removed' rows, TA-IDX-REPORT for already-announced events (MRNA, RX.V).

When a base close is not stored (rows before 2026-10-29) the 5-session return falls back to the stored measures.return_5d_pct on the end-session row, which is the same close-to-close return by definition.
